Treatment failure, so repeat benzathine penicillin G immediately
Chorioamnionitis, so start broad antibiotics and deliver
items.explanation: Fever, myalgias, contractions, and fetal heart rate changes within hours of the first syphilis treatment represent a Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction from release of spirochete products. It is more frequent in early syphilis, and it is managed with antipyretics and fetal monitoring while treatment continues. Anaphylaxis would bring hives, wheeze, or hypotension. Treatment failure cannot be judged within hours, and chorioamnionitis would not follow a penicillin dose so closely.

items.stem: During a vaginal birth at 41 weeks of a fetus estimated at 4,300 g, shoulder dystocia is recognized. McRoberts positioning and suprapubic pressure have both been tried for a minute without success. What is the most appropriate next maneuver?
options: Fundal pressure by an assistant
Zavanelli maneuver with immediate cesarean
Symphysiotomy at the bedside
Delivery of the posterior arm
items.explanation: When first-line maneuvers fail, the next step is an internal maneuver: delivering the posterior arm, or rotational maneuvers such as Rubin or Woods screw. Delivering the posterior arm reduces the shoulder diameter. Fundal pressure worsens impaction and is contraindicated. Zavanelli and symphysiotomy are last-resort rescue measures used only after all other options fail, never first.

items.stem: A 30-year-old at 20 weeks has an anatomy scan showing a fetus with a lemon-shaped skull, banana-shaped cerebellum, and a lumbosacral defect. Which maternal measure before conception could have reduced this risk?
options: Daily low-dose aspirin from the first trimester
Vitamin A supplementation at 10,000 IU daily
Folic acid 0.4 mg daily starting at least one month before conception
Iron supplementation at 60 mg daily
items.explanation: The lemon and banana signs identify open spina bifida, a neural tube defect; folic acid 0.4 mg daily lowers occurrence by up to 70 percent, and 4 mg is used for a prior affected pregnancy. Aspirin helps prevent preeclampsia. Excess vitamin A is teratogenic. Iron prevents anemia but has no effect on neural tube closure.

items.stem: A 28-year-old at 38 weeks has a spinal anesthetic for cesarean delivery and becomes hypotensive to 78/40 mm Hg with nausea. Which agent is the first-line treatment?
options: Atropine
Epinephrine
Ephedrine in a large single dose
Phenylephrine
items.explanation: Neuraxial sympathetic blockade causes vasodilation; phenylephrine, an alpha agonist, restores vascular tone without the fetal acidosis seen with ephedrine, and left uterine displacement with fluid also helps. Atropine treats bradycardia rather than vasodilation. Epinephrine is reserved for refractory shock. Ephedrine crosses the placenta and is associated with lower umbilical pH. Fluid preloading and left uterine displacement reduce, but rarely prevent, this common hypotension.

items.stem: A 31-year-old, 2 weeks postpartum and breastfeeding, has dyspnea, orthopnea, and an ejection fraction of 30 percent. She is on a loop diuretic and a beta blocker. Which agent should be added for afterload reduction?
options: Enalapril
Sacubitril-valsartan
Losartan
Amlodipine
items.explanation: Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors are contraindicated in pregnancy but are standard for peripartum cardiomyopathy after delivery, and enalapril and captopril have the best lactation safety data. Sacubitril-valsartan and the angiotensin receptor blockers lack adequate data during breastfeeding. Amlodipine lowers pressure but has no outcome benefit in systolic heart failure. Blood pressure and renal function should be checked within a week of starting the drug, as with any such agent.

items.stem: A 26-year-old G2P1 at 29 weeks has regular contractions every 5 minutes, a cervix dilated 3 cm and 80 percent effaced, and intact membranes. She has no bleeding, fever, or fetal compromise. Which management is most appropriate?
options: Prolonged tocolysis with indomethacin until 36 weeks
Corticosteroids and magnesium neuroprotection
Strict bed rest and intravenous hydration alone
Maintenance terbutaline for the rest of the pregnancy
items.explanation: Preterm labor before 34 weeks calls for antenatal corticosteroids to mature the fetal lungs, with magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection when delivery is imminent before 32 weeks, and transfer to a center with a neonatal unit if needed. Short tocolysis may buy time for steroids, but prolonged tocolysis does not improve outcomes. Bed rest and hydration do not stop labor, and maintenance terbutaline is ineffective and unsafe.
